articles.title: Ministério Público acusa formalmente Santiago Peña no Paraguai | G1
articles.standfirst: Cassado pelo Senado, ele é investigado por suposto envolvimento na crise do Banco Ueno. Promotores também pediram prisão preventiva do ex-presidente.
articles.summary: Cassado pelo Senado, ele é investigado por suposto envolvimento na crise do Banco Ueno. Promotores também pediram prisão preventiva do ex-presidente.
articles.body:
No terceiro dia de crise no Paraguai, o Ministério Público apresentou acusação formal contra o ex-presidente Santiago Peña por envolvimento no colapso do Banco Ueno.

Santiago Peña chegou de madrugada numa base militar de elite em Assunção, capital do país.

Ele teve detenção temporária domiciliar decretada na noite desta sexta-feira (6), mas foi transferido por questões de segurança.

Isso porque manifestantes que estavam na porta da casa dele acabaram entrando em confronto com a polícia. Um policial ficou ferido.

A confusão foi logo após a longa sessão do Senado que cassou o mandato de Peña.

Na quinta-feira (5), o então presidente havia pedido a renúncia do cargo, na tentativa de obter imunidade parlamentar como senador vitalício, mas o pedido foi rejeitado pelo Congresso paraguaio.

A decisão pelo impeachment foi aprovada por unanimidade pelos 44 senadores presentes nesta sexta. Um parlamentar não compareceu.

Neste sábado (7) pela manhã, Santiago Peña se apresentou para prestar depoimento à Procuradoria-Geral do Ministério Público do país.

À tarde, os promotores formalizaram a acusação por abuso de confiança e administração em benefício próprio e pediram a prisão preventiva do ex-presidente do Paraguai .

A mudança do regime de prisão ainda depende da decisão da Justiça. Santiago Peña nega os crimes.

A acusação faz parte das investigações sobre o caso do banco digital Ueno, o centro dessa crise política.

Até o ano passado, Peña era sócio do grupo controlador da instituição e nomeou o ex-diretor do Ueno, Carlos Carvallo, para a presidência do Banco Central Paraguaio. Ele também está detido.

O Banco Ueno enfrenta problemas financeiros e é alvo de investigações.

Nesta semana, interrompeu o acesso de correntistas ao dinheiro depositado depois de uma intervenção da autoridade monetária do país.

Nas ruas, após o impeachment, a população pede agora o ressarcimento financeiro das contas congeladas.

Este sábado também foi o primeiro dia de governo do novo presidente no poder: Pedro Allana, também do Partido Colorado, e que ocupava o cargo de vice.

Formado em relações internacionais, ele tem 52 anos e já foi deputado e governador. O novo presidente começou os trabalhos por volta das 6h, segundo a imprensa local.

O dia foi marcado por uma série de reuniões com ministros que faziam parte do governo de Peña. Apesar disso, mudanças ministeriais ainda não foram anunciadas.

Agora há pouco, a Justiça do Paraguai aceitou o pedido do Ministério Público e converteu a prisão do ex-presidente Santiago Peña para preventiva.

Ministério Público acusa formalmente Santiago Peña no Paraguai — Foto: Jornal Nacional

articles.title: Eventos bloqueiam orla de Santos e alteram linhas de ônibus domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Bloqueios começam às 4h e seguem até as 12h, dependendo do trecho. Interdições serão realizadas para corrida, Batalha dos Garçons e DiversaCaminhada.
articles.summary: Bloqueios começam às 4h e seguem até as 12h, dependendo do trecho. Interdições serão realizadas para corrida, Batalha dos Garçons e DiversaCaminhada.
articles.body:
Santos terá interdições de trânsito na orla por causa de diversos eventos. — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/A Tribuna Jornal

A orla de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, terá alterações no trânsito e no transporte público neste domingo (8) devido à realização de três eventos: campeonato de pedestrianismo , DiversaCaminhada e Batalha dos Garçons ( veja abaixo ).

Os bloqueios começam às 4h e podem seguir até as 12h , dependendo do trecho interditado.

Segundo a Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET-Santos), as i nterdições atingirão cinco avenidas , principalmente no sentido José Menino/Ponta da Praia. Ao todo, dez linhas municipais de ônibus terão desvios temporários.

As interdições também provocarão desvios temporários em dez linhas do transporte coletivo municipal. Confira os itinerários alternativos:

Linha 07 ( sentido José Menino/Boqueirão ): Avenida Presidente Wilson, Avenida Senador Pinheiro Machado, Rua Marechal Floriano Peixoto, Avenida Ana Costa, Praça da Independência, Rua Galeão Carvalhal, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo e Avenida Conselheiro Nébias (sentido Praia/Centro).

Linha 17 ( sentido Gonzaga/Boqueirão ): Avenida Bernardino de Campos, Rua Marechal Floriano Peixoto, Avenida Ana Costa, Praça da Independência, Rua Galeão Carvalhal, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo, Avenida Epitácio Pessoa e Avenida Siqueira Campos (sentido Praia/Centro).

Linhas 23, 52 e 152 ( sentido José Menino/Ponta da Praia ): Avenida Presidente Wilson, Avenida Senador Pinheiro Machado, Rua Marechal Floriano Peixoto, Avenida Ana Costa, Praça da Independência, Rua Galeão Carvalhal, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo, Avenida Epitácio Pessoa, Avenida Rei Alberto I e Praça Gago Coutinho.

Linha 42 ( sentido Gonzaga/Ponta da Praia ): Praça da Independência, Rua Galeão Carvalhal, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo, Avenida Epitácio Pessoa, Avenida Rei Alberto I e Praça Gago Coutinho.

Linhas 05 e 139 ( sentido Gonzaga/BNH ): Praça da Independência, Rua Galeão Carvalhal, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo, Avenida Epitácio Pessoa e Rua Alexandre Martins.

Linha 154 ( sentido Gonzaga/Boqueirão ): Praça da Independência, Rua Galeão Carvalhal, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo e Avenida Conselheiro Nébias (sentido Praia/Centro).

Linha 184 ( sentido Gonzaga/BNH ): Avenida Conselheiro Nébias, Rua Heitor de Moraes, Rua Roberto Simonsen, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo, Avenida Epitácio Pessoa e Rua Alexandre Martins.

Linha 194 ( sentido Canal 2/Ponta da Praia ): Avenida Presidente Wilson, Avenida Ana Costa, Praça da Independência, Rua Galeão Carvalhal, Rua Governador Pedro de Toledo, Avenida Epitácio Pessoa, Avenida Rei Alberto I e Praça Gago Coutinho.

A quinta e última etapa do 39º Campeonato Santista de Pedestrianismo será realizada a partir das 7h, com largada na Avenida Vicente de Carvalho, em frente à Praça das Bandeiras.

A prova é promovida em parceria com o 6º Batalhão de Polícia Militar do Interior (6º BPM/I) e integra a 22ª Corrida do Batalhão.

A competição será realizada das 9h às 11h, na Avenida Bartolomeu de Gusmão, em frente à Praça do Aquário, na Ponta da Praia.

O evento reunirá 44 profissionais da gastronomia em uma corrida com bandejas. A entrada é gratuita e haverá mais de R$ 10 mil em prêmios.

A concentração da 2ª DiversaCaminhada começa às 10h, na Fonte do Sapo, no bairro Aparecida, com saída prevista para as 11h. O percurso terá aproximadamente 2,2 quilômetros pela orla, em direção à Concha Acústica, no Canal 3.

A programação contará com minitrio elétrico, apresentação da DJ Nicolly LeBlanc e performances do coletivo House of DDD. A atividade integra a programação da 9ª Parada do Orgulho LGBT+ de Santos.

articles.title: Emprega Prudente oferece quase 500 vagas de emprego; confira | G1
articles.standfirst: Vagas estão distribuídas entre as áreas de comércio, indústria e serviços. Há oportunidades para profissionais com ensino superior.
articles.summary: O Emprega Prudente, programa da Prefeitura de Presidente Prudente (SP), está com 493 vagas de emprego disponíveis até a última atualização, neste sábado (7).
articles.body:
Para se inscrever, é possível acessar o site ou comparecer na unidade do Atende Prudente — Foto: Arquivo/Secom

O programa Emprega Prudente está com 493 vagas de emprego disponíveis em Presidente Prudente (SP), conforme atualização deste sábado (7).

As oportunidades são para diferentes áreas, com destaque para o comércio e serviços.

Também há oportunidades para profissionais de diferentes níveis técnicos, desde fundamental ao curso superior. Confira abaixo:

Interessados com nível fundamental completo e incompleto: 315 vagas;

ensino médio/técnico completo e incompleto: 168 vagas;

superior completo e incompleto: 10 vagas;

pessoas com deficiência (PcD): 22 vagas.

Todas as vagas podem ser consultadas no Mural de Vagas do site Prudente Digital ou presencialmente na unidade do Atende Prudente, Rua Marechal Floriano Peixoto, 342, Vila Marcondes.

Também é possível confirmar outros detalhes pelo telefone do Atende Prudente: (18) 3399-1100.

articles.title: Cabos irregulares em Ribeirão Preto: 21,5 toneladas são retiradas | G1
articles.standfirst: Força-tarefa entre Prefeitura, CPFL e operadoras tenta conter riscos de acidentes e poluição visual nos postes da cidade. Desde 2021, concessionária registrou mais de 18 mil chamados por fios soltos.
articles.summary: Cabos irregulares em Ribeirão Preto somam 21 toneladas recolhidas em ação contra fios soltos; veja como denunciar riscos e quem são os responsáveis pela rede.
articles.body:
Equipes de fiscalização recolheram 21,5 toneladas de cabos de telecomunicações irregulares, clandestinos e abandonados dos postes de iluminação pública em Ribeirão Preto (SP) entre janeiro e novembro de 2026.

A ação faz parte de uma força-tarefa da Comissão de Infraestrutura Aérea de Ribeirão Preto (Coinfarp), composta pela Prefeitura, pela concessionária CPFL Paulista e por empresas de telefonia e internet. O objetivo é eliminar riscos de acidentes com pedestres e motociclistas, além de combater a poluição visual urbana.

Na última quinta-feira (5), os trabalhos de limpeza e readequação concentraram-se na Avenida Presidente Vargas, uma das principais vias da zona Sul da cidade. Somente em 2026, vistorias técnicas mapearam 381 postes com ocupação clandestina e outros 904 pontos com cabos sem a identificação obrigatória das operadoras .

Em nota, a CPFL Paulista informou que cumpre as normas de compartilhamento fixadas pelos órgãos reguladores e que notifica as operadoras para a regularização dos fios. A Conexis Brasil Digital, entidade que representa as maiores operadoras de telecomunicações, afirma que as empresas credenciadas investem continuamente na manutenção e limpeza das redes alugadas.

Operário retira fiação solta de poste em Ribeirão Preto (SP). — Foto: Serginho Oliveira/EPTV

A consultora de relacionamento da CPFL Paulista, Elidiane Bernardi, destaca que a prioridade das operações é a segurança da população nas vias públicas.

"O real trabalho aqui é focado na questão da segurança. Não é só uma questão de estética. Primeiramente é a segurança, para que os cabos estejam de acordo com o que regem as normas e a regulamentação da Anatel e da Aneel. Depois que estão de forma segura, entra a questão estética e o que for possível reduzir de cabo a gente faz", afirma a consultora.

O que são cabos clandestinos, irregulares e mortos?

A fiscalização divide os problemas encontrados nos postes nas seguintes categorias:

🔍 Ocupação à revelia ou clandestina : instalação de cabos feita por empresas sem contrato assinado com a concessionária detentora dos postes.

🔍 Fiação irregular : ocorre quando a operadora tem contrato de uso com a distribuidora, mas instalou cabos em pontos não autorizados ou fora das normas técnicas.

🔍 Cabo morto ou abandonado : fiação desativada e sem uso que deixou de ser retirada pela operadora, gerando sobrepeso na estrutura e risco de queda.

Funcionários trabalham na organização de fiação em postes de Ribeirão Preto (SP). — Foto: Serginho Oliveira/EPTV

A responsabilidade sobre a estrutura dos postes é compartilhada entre diferentes agentes públicos e privados, de acordo com regras federais e municipais:

CPFL Paulista : é a proprietária dos postes. Cabe à concessionária gerenciar o aluguel dos espaços, fiscalizar o cumprimento das normas de segurança e notificar as operadoras em caso de irregularidades.

Empresas de telefonia e internet : são as donas dos cabos. Elas pagam aluguel à CPFL para utilizar a infraestrutura e têm a obrigação de manter os fios alinhados, identificados com placa contendo nome e telefone, além de retirar cabos desativados.

Prefeitura de Ribeirão Preto : atua na coordenação do cronograma de limpeza por meio da Coinfarp, fiscaliza o cumprimento da legislação municipal e encaminha as denúncias feitas pelos moradores para a concessionária.

As vistorias são feitas periodicamente por técnicos da CPFL Paulista. Quando uma fiação irregular é detectada, a concessionária emite uma notificação formal estipulando prazo para que a operadora ajuste a fiação.

Se o problema não for corrigido dentro do prazo, a operadora fica sujeita a sanções contratuais, multas e à remoção forçada dos cabos.

Em situações emergenciais, como fios caídos na pista, cabos energizados ou fiações clandestinas sem contrato, a distribuidora tem autorização legal para realizar o corte imediato sem aviso prévio, a fim de evitar tragédias.

Um dos desafios das operações de limpeza é a fiação clandestina emaranhada às redes regulares.

Em outubro de 2026, a retirada emergencial de fiação irregular no bairro City Ribeirão provocou a interrupção acidental da internet em escritórios e espaços de coworking, paralisando serviços ao longo do dia.

O diretor de tecnologia da provedora Alcans, Cláudio Placa, explica que a presença de empresas clandestinas nos postes dificulta a identificação visual no momento da limpeza.

"Quando os provedores não regularizados ocupam o poste, eles embolam os fios. Na hora da limpeza, a equipe puxa e acaba rompendo cabos regulares junto. Nossas equipes trabalham 24 horas e, quando há rompimento acidental durante o serviço da distribuidora, fazemos o suporte para restabelecer o sinal no menor tempo possível", afirma o diretor.

O empresário Robinson Cardoso, que teve a rotina administrativa paralisada durante o incidente no bairro City Ribeirão, cobra mais transparência nas operações.

"Nossa operação depende 100% da internet. Falta uma comunicação clara entre Prefeitura, CPFL e operadoras para que os empresários e clientes sejam avisados com antecedência quando houver manutenção, evitando prejuízos", ressalta o empresário.

Como os moradores podem denunciar fios soltos ou caídos?

Caso o morador identifique cabos pendurados, caídos na calçada ou com altura abaixo do permitido sobre a rua (mínimo de 5 metros de altura), o registro pode ser feito diretamente pelos canais oficiais:

Prefeitura de Ribeirão Preto : pelo telefone 156 ou pelo aplicativo SAM (Serviço de Atendimento ao Munícipe). A demanda é registrada e repassada à comissão de fiscalização.

CPFL Paulista : pelo telefone 0800 010 1010 (central gratuita de atendimento).

As autoridades alertam que a população nunca deve tentar puxar, cortar ou encostar em cabos pendurados nos postes, pois há risco de a fiação de telefonia ter entrado em contato com a rede de alta tensão elétrica.

Emaranhado de fiações polui paisagem urbana e causa transtornos a moradores de Ribeirão Preto (SP). — Foto: Serginho Oliveira/EPTV

VÍDEOS: Tudo sobre Ribeirão Preto, Franca e região

articles.title: Israel: Líder da oposição tem chance de formar governo e substituir Netanyahu | G1
articles.standfirst: Gadi Eisenkot recebeu do presidente a missão de formar uma coalizão com maioria no Parlamento e pode encerrar o governo de Benjamin Netanyahu após anos no poder.
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot recebeu do presidente a missão de formar uma coalizão com maioria no Parlamento e pode encerrar o governo de Benjamin Netanyahu após anos no poder.
articles.body:
Em Israel, o líder da oposição recebeu a tarefa de formar um novo governo com uma coalizão parlamentar. Se conseguir, pode tirar Benjamin Netanyahu do cargo de primeiro-ministro.

A decisão foi anunciada depois que as eleições israelenses de 27 de outubro terminaram sem um vencedor claro.

Agora, Gadi Eisenkot, líder do partido Yashar, de oposição ao primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, vai assumir a responsabilidade de formar uma coalizão .

Se o atual primeiro-ministro deixar o cargo, perderá a imunidade parlamentar e poderá ser investigado por corrupção.

Netanyahu responde a acusações de fraude, quebra de confiança e suborno relacionadas ao recebimento de presentes e supostas negociações de favores em troca de cobertura de imprensa favorável.

Israel é parlamentarista. O presidente tem função principalmente cerimonial, mas é ele quem nomeia o chefe do governo, levando em conta o resultado das urnas.

A imprensa israelense informou que o presidente Herzog recebeu 67 recomendações para nomear o líder da oposição. Benjamin Netanyahu teria recebido 46 indicações.

A partir de amanhã, Eisenkot terá o prazo de 28 dias, prorrogáveis por mais 14, para formar a nova coalizão.

Nesse período, Eisenkot terá que fechar alianças para ter apoio de ao menos 61 das 120 cadeiras no Congresso. A tarefa não será fácil.

O Yashar, de Eisenkot, conseguiu sozinho apenas 21 assentos. O Likud, de Netanyahu, obteve um pouco mais: 27 cadeiras.

A chave para a vitória pode ser uma antes improvável coalizão com os árabes, que chegaram a um recorde de 19 parlamentares eleitos.

Independentemente do futuro do governo israelense, o novo primeiro-ministro já começará com um grande desafio: o corte no apoio financeiro americano aos militares israelenses .

No dia da eleição para o Congresso americano, o presidente Donald Trump anunciou que cortaria a ajuda anual de US$ 4 bilhões a Israel.

Israel: Líder da oposição tem chance de formar governo e substituir Netanyahu — Foto: Jornal Nacional

articles.title: New mass protests in France as police thwart banned rally
articles.summary: Thousands of people protested across France on Saturday in a new show of anger against the government with Paris police moving to prevent an unauthorised gat...
articles.body:
Thousands of people protested across France on Saturday in a new show of anger against the government with Paris police moving to prevent an unauthorised gathering near the president's Elysee Palace office and residence.

The protests mark the fourth weekend in a row of demonstrations, which have erupted as the country tilts towards presidential elections in five months' time in which the far right sees its best chance yet to win power.

Authorities expected up to 170,000 people to protest nationwide, including 60,000 in Paris. But the interior ministry counted 7,000 people protesting early afternoon nationwide, down on the same time last week and indicating a downward trend in participation, an official told AFP.

The demonstrations come after mass protests by unions on Thursday accompanied by strikes, with teaching unions vowing more walk-outs next week.

Some 70,000 members of the security forces were deployed Saturday, ready to move in quickly after mass protests on October 17 degenerated into the worst riots seen in France in years.

Unions staged a march along a traditional route, from the Place de la Republique in central Paris to Place de la Nation in the east of the city.

But the Yellow Vests movement -- a group whose protests shook Emmanuel Macron in the early years of his presidency almost a decade ago -- called for a rival demonstration at the Place de la Concorde in central Paris, a stone's throw from the president's Elysee Palace and the lower house of parliament.

This action has been banned by the authorities, and on Saturday a large police presence prevented protesters from getting close. Some 100 people who arrived were surrounded by police and one of the movement's coordinators, Benjamin Ball, and its spokeswoman, Azelma Sigaux, were apprehended by police, an AFP reporter said.

In the southeastern city of Lyon, police fired tear gas to disperse several hundred people in the city centre blocking a road during an unauthorised gathering.

"The risk is exactly the same as on previous Saturdays," said Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, calling on authorities "not to lower their guard".

The wave of demonstrations was sparked by a movement in late September by high school students angered by conditions at their establishments. These teens, joined by university students, remain at the heart of the protests.

"Today is a date that helps keep the pressure on," said Sabine Kharbach, spokeswoman of the Student Union. "Many young people are mobilising because the government's responses remain unsatisfactory."

The police response has faced criticism for being heavy-handed, with dozens of internal investigations launched into allegations of brutality against demonstrators.

After several instances of apparent police brutality against AFP reporters covering the protests, the international news agency on Friday urged protection for its journalists.

Local businesses are also feeling the pain. "So this can't go on, otherwise I think it will be a disaster before long," said Paris shop manager Jean Emile Moulinier, whose store is around the main protest route and says hardly any customers brave security barricades on protest weekends.

Shop windows of stores in Paris and other cities were again barricaded with wooden shutters and often closed for the day to prevent potential ransacking.

The government is grappling with ways to find solutions but is constrained by France's gigantic debt pile which is already spooking markets.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is due to meet unions and employer federation representatives on Monday to discuss wages and purchasing power.

But student and teacher groups in France have called for a new strike on Tuesday to keep pressure on the government for more education spending, saying they were "in a position of strength (and) the government in a position of weakness and starting to yield".

Polls meanwhile show that far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the favourite to win the Elysee in 2027 with her main rival currently not one of Macron's centrist former allies but hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon.

Melenchon was due to address a rally later Saturday.

images.caption: There were protests nationwide in France (Philippe LOPEZ)

articles.title: Rep.-elect Ojeda posts tribute to father who died after midterms: ‘He held on’
articles.summary: Democratic North Carolina Rep.-elect Richard Ojeda on Friday posted a tribute for his late father who passed away following the Democrat’s win in the midterm...
articles.body:
Democratic North Carolina Rep.-elect Richard Ojeda on Friday posted a tribute for his late father who passed away following the Democrat's win in the midterm elections.

"For years, my dad battled Parkinson's disease. On Election Night, I got to tell him, "Pop, we won." This morning, he passed away," Ojeda wrote in post on social platform X on Friday.

"A part of me believes he held on just long enough to see his son make it to Congress. He won't be there when I'm sworn in. But I know he'll be standing right beside me," the newly elected congressman added.

Ojeda defeated Rep. Richard Hudson (R), the chair of the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC), in a close race for North Carolina's 9th Congressional District which includes Hoke, Moore, Randolph and Alamance counties, along with portions of Guilford, Cumberland and Chatham counties.

The Democrat eked out a victory with more than 51 percent votes while the Republican incumbent secured a little less than 49 percent of the votes, according to Decision Desk HQ . His victory marks the first Democratic win in the district since 1963.

North Carolina's flipped seat in the 9th Congressional District was in line with the Democrats' sweeping victory in the midterm elections where they took control of both the House and the Senate, securing major wins in battleground states across the country.

In another post on Friday night on social platform X, said his father, "Richard Neece Ojeda lived an extraordinary life" and he "traveled the world and lived a life of service that started in the US Air Force and continued after graduating from the Mayo Clinic where he was commissioned as an officer in the US Army."

He noted that his father spent 55 years after his military service practicing anesthesia and was the "first man in Logan County history to perform an epidural at Logan Regional Hospital in Logan, WV."

In his morning post, Ojeda dedicated his Congressional victory to his father saying, "Rest easy, Daddy. I'll take it from here. These next two years are for you."

articles.title: After Trump made inroads, Latinos help Democrats deliver blue wave
articles.summary: Hispanic Americans helped deliver a historic blow to the GOP in Tuesday’s contest, diminishing gains President Trump made with Latino men while augmenting the ranks of Democrats in the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC). Exit polling data from polling firm BSP showed significant attrition among Latinos who backed Trump in 2024 — 17 percent of those…
articles.body:
Hispanic Americans helped deliver a historic blow to the GOP in Tuesday’s contest, diminishing gains President Trump made with Latino men while augmenting the ranks of Democrats in the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC).

Exit polling data from polling firm BSP showed significant attrition among Latinos who backed Trump in 2024 — 17 percent of those who backed the president in the last election cycle supported the Democratic ticket during the midterms.

Meanwhile, a record-breaking number of Latinos voted this week, including newer, younger voters who more consistently backed the Democratic ticket. BSP found that among Latinos casting a ballot, 17 percent were first-time federal election voters, while 41 percent had joined the electorate since the 2022 cycle.

“While the numbers are still coming in, what we know so far indicates that this will undoubtedly be the largest turnout of Latino voters ever in a midterm election,” Janet Murguía, president and CEO of Unidos US, said on a call with reporters.

“It’s estimated that as many as 14.5 million Hispanics went to the polls, and I can’t help but reflect on the fact that President Trump asked voters across the country to pretend like he was on the ballot, and our observation is that Latino voters did just that by resoundingly rejecting his extreme policies and actions and anyone who rubber-stamped them.”

The group’s voting power was seen not just in how it voted but in who is ascending to public office.

The Congressional Hispanic Caucus — the group of Democratic Latino lawmakers serving in Congress — said its membership will swell to 56 members just in time for its 50th anniversary.

“This is an exciting year to see that our ranks are growing in that manner,” outgoing CHC Chair Adriano Espaillat (D-N.Y.) told The Hill, going on to note that many of the mid-decade redistricting efforts driven by the GOP threatened seats held by Latino members.

“We felt that because of the stuff that went on with the Republicans and redistricting, that we may lose seats, and it was sort of the other way around. We gained them, or we overperformed.”

In some cases, new members flipped seats held by Hispanic Republicans or even ousted Democratic Hispanic incumbents. Others have won seats not previously held by Latinos.

In total the caucus has 16 new members, expanding its size by 12 lawmakers.

Latinos voters were also key in delivering Democratic victories in GOP strongholds like Texas, which Trump carried decisively in 2024 but now has a blue senator and elected Gina Hinojosa (D) to serve as the state’s first Latina governor.

Data from The Associated Press found roughly 7 in 10 Hispanic voters supported Texas Democrat James Talarico in the U.S. Senate contest, while only about 3 in 10 voted for Republican Ken Paxton. When Trump was on the ballot last cycle, Texas Latinos had evenly split their support in the presidential race.

Polling also shows that Latino voters, like many others casting ballots Tuesday, were motivated by concerns over the high cost of living.

Gary Segura, president at polling firm BSP, said data showed that just 15 percent of Hispanics they polled described their financial situation as “comfortable” and just a third said they have “some left over” after paying bills.

“Half of the Latino population have nothing left over after they pay their bills, or in fact might even be struggling to make their bills each month, and more than 4 in 10 expect that the continuation of Trump economic policies would make them worse off in the next year,” he told reporters.

Other data analyzed by his firm showed just how alienated Latinos have become with the GOP.

Sixty-four percent of those polled said they had an unfavorable opinion about Trump and were broadly negative about the GOP.

“Nearly two-thirds say Democrats care a great deal about the Latino community, while about 7 in 10 say Republicans don’t care or are actively hostile,” Segura said.

There’s no doubt immigration played a significant role in shaping Latino attitudes heading into the election.

“For a long time, I believe that immigration was sort of like a taboo issue,” Espaillat said, arguing that many Democrats felt there was little change of passing immigration reform.

“Once ICE [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] came in and did what they’re doing, it was pretty much in everybody’s view what was happening. And I think that the aggressiveness of ICE, the detentions, the deportations, the killings, and the whole really traumatic experience that the country has lived through with ICE on the streets of our nation had a dramatic impact on Latino voters coming out.”

“Latino voters overwhelmingly want an immigration system that includes a path to citizenship,” he said.

Seventy-six percent of those polled said they want ICE reforms, while 68 percent “want that blank check written to ICE pulled back.”

Several Latinos have been among those shot and killed by immigration officers within the first two years of Trump’s second term, including the deaths of Johan Sebastian Guerrero in Maine and Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas. Marimar Martinez , who lived after being shot at five times by an officer in Illinois, has spoken out about aggressive immigration enforcement.

More than 60 people have also died in immigration detention since Trump took office.

Murguía said for many Latino voters, the issue is one they’ve experienced within their own circles.

“Many of the folks I talked to had stories about the run-ins they, their family members, neighbors, even those who are citizens have had with immigration enforcement officers. They also told me about the toll that mass deportation was taking on businesses and neighborhoods definitely having a negative economic impact,” she said.

But experts caution that Latinos want nuance in border and immigration policy, a factor that helped Trump gain some support with the group in 2024.

Segura posed a vision he said had broad appeal.

“We read the following policy … ‘We need a balanced and orderly immigration system that has an earned path to citizenship for long-term residents, focuses enforcement inside the country on keeping communities safe with clear accountability, offers legal ways to immigrate that help economy and families and keeps the border secure.’ Ninety percent of Latinos agree with that,” he said.

Latino leaders have long argued neither party should take its voters for granted, arguing Hispanics are heavily motivated by issues.

Murguía said the midterms also spurred some of the highest levels of outreach to Latino voters.

“We hope both parties will take away the lesson that outreach matters,” she said.

“We believe that the results in 2024 and now 2026 will finally convince elected officials and the political establishment that Latinos are indeed a swing vote.”

articles.title: Sunday shows preview: Democrats lay out legislative agenda; Congress leadership sparks infighting
articles.summary: With Democrats set to take control of both the House and Senate following sweeping victories in the midterm elections, sitting lawmakers have already begun to lay out plans for the lame-duck period and the latter half of President Trump’s second term. Democrats secured big wins in battleground states, flipping GOP-held seats in places like Texas,…
articles.body:
With Democrats set to take control of both the House and Senate following sweeping victories in the midterm elections, sitting lawmakers have already begun to lay out plans for the lame-duck period and the latter half of President Trump’s second term.

Democrats secured big wins in battleground states , flipping GOP-held seats in places like Texas, Maine, Kansas, Iowa, South Carolina and Ohio. With 54 Senate and 254 House seat — and other races yet to be decided — the Democratic Party is already setting the stage for clashes with GOP officials in the Trump administration.

Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee who’s seeking to chair the panel, issued a two-word statement to Trump officials after the blue wave: “Lawyer up.” Garcia is set to appear on CNN’s “State of the Union” Sunday.

Democrats, and as well as some Republican lawmakers, have also called for the impeachment of top Trump administration officials, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Two House Democrats , Reps. Hank Johnson (Ga.) and Deborah Ross (N.C.), voiced their support Thursday for impeachment efforts against these GOP administrators in an interview with SiriusXM’s “The Dan Abrams Show.”

Blanche is expected to appear in Fox News’s “Fox News Sunday.”

The calls for Hegseth’s removal came from both sides of the aisles, with Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) telling CNN he plans to call for a vote to impeach the defense secretary. The Kentucky Republican later posted on social media saying his impeachment resolution is “ a much gentler version of what’s coming when Dem’s control Congress. They’ll have hearings & trials.”

In response , Hegseth said in a Thursday video posted to social platform X, “A disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies, has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly.”

President Trump asked the Department of Justice Saturday to investigate Democrats’ investigation threats toward administration officials, calling them “extortion at the highest level.”

Though the White House announced its own leadership shake-ups after Election Day. On Friday, the president announced his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, was leaving the White House and longtime adviser Stephen Miller would take her place. Prior to this, former White House adviser Steve Bannon called for Wiles’s immediate removal due to the GOP’s midterm shellacking.

Party officials were quick to place blame on issues like cost of living and the ongoing war in Iran for Republican losses. Even Vice President Vance, attributed the widespread defeat to the administration’s war with the Islamic Republic.

Republican Sen. Ted Cruz (Texas) pointed to cost of living as a “top issue” after the Lone Star State witnessed a historic flip — with state Rep. Gina Hinojosa (D) defeating incumbent GOP Gov. Greg Abbott and Democrat James Talarico beating state Attorney General Ken Paxton (R) in the Senate race.

Despite facing unprecedented losses in several historically red-leaning states, the GOP maintained its strong hold in states like Florida , where Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.) defeated Democrat David Jolly in the gubernatorial race. Donalds is set to appear on NBC News’s “Meet the Press” and Fox News’s “Sunday Morning Futures.”

The stunning midterms results also heated up leadership conversations for the 120th Congress. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) is expected to run for the position of the minority leader, a source familiar with his plans told The Hill , where he will likely face against House Judiciary Committee Chair Jim Jordan (R-Ohio). This came after Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said on a staff call Wednesday that he will not run for the post .

On the Democratic side, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) is on track to take the majority leader post. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (N.Y.) also announced he would seek reelection as Senate majority leader. However, newly elected Democratic senators, including Abdul El-Sayed (Mich.) and Adam Hamilton (Kan.) said they would not cast their votes for him.

Hamilton is set to appear on NBC News’s “Meet the Press” and CNN’s “State of the Union.”

See the full list of guests on the Sunday morning news shows below:

CBS News’s “Face the Nation”: Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Rep. French Hill (R-Ark.), Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore (D-S.C.).

CNN’s “State of the Union”: Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton (D-Kan.), Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.).

Fox News’s “Fox News Sunday”: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D).

NBC News’s “Meet the Press”: Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton (D-Kan.), Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds (R), Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro (D).

Fox News’s “Sunday Morning Futures”: Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds (R), Tennessee Sen. Bill Hagerty (R), Former Deputy Treasury Secretary Michael Faulkender, Former Speaker Newt Gingrich (R-Ga.).

articles.title: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
articles.summary: Republicans can stick with Trumpism or chart a new path, writes BBC Washington correspondent Daniel Bush.
articles.body:
Republicans are in soul-searching mode after the coalition that powered Donald Trump to three straight presidential nominations imploded in spectacular fashion in the 2026 midterms.

The stunning election defeat immediately raised questions about the party's future post-Trump.

But there are no easy answers as Republicans face the choice of doubling down on Trumpism or trying to chart a new path forward in his final years in office.

The depth of the problem was captured by outgoing Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who called the midterms "close to an extinction-level event for Republicans".

Others struck a more optimistic tone. Vice-President JD Vance, who blamed the midterm results on public anger over the war with Iran, argued the party could turn things around. Nevertheless Vance acknowledged the fallout will be messy.

"There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why," Vance said.

The wide range of reactions on the right highlights deep fault lines in the party that formed around Trump's improbable rise to the presidency in 2016 and never really went away.

It's too early to tell which faction will win out. But while Republicans are still licking their wounds, the intraparty battle Vance predicted is already under way.

The party must decide whether it will be "centred on one figure, one guy, or on a wider set of ideas like conservatism that can win outside the deepest red places," Rina Shah, a Republican strategist, told the BBC.

Critics on the right - the "Never Trumpers" who opposed his first White House campaign - are pushing for a return to the Republican Party's pre-Trump roots, citing the historic losses around the country on election night.

But simply turning back the clock on Trump will be extremely difficult if not impossible to do.

The party has been wholly transformed during Trump's decade-long reign. Most Republicans have shifted to the right on domestic issues like immigration, and rejected the interventionist foreign policy of the George W Bush era that led to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.

In Congress, the more moderate establishment wing of the party that disliked Trump from the start has almost entirely disappeared, replaced by conservative Trump backers who echo his nativism and populist rhetoric.

That trend continued this year, as old-guard Republicans like John Cornyn in Texas and Maine's Susan Collins, both of whom clashed with Trump over the years, were voted out of office.

Three days after the election Trump appointed Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff , replacing Susie Wiles.

The move signalled Trump has no plans to moderate his policies or message in his remaining years in office. Miller, who had been serving as the president's chief domestic policy adviser, is a longtime Trump aide known for his hardline immigration policies.

With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle

One of the architects of the Make America Great Again (Maga) movement, Steve Bannon, predicted a "civil war" in the party after the midterms.

Afterwards, he blamed the Republicans' defeat on the economy and "foreign wars". "I don't think we implemented the Maga programme," he said, calling on Trump to double down on mass deportations.

But other Republican strategists said the midterms were a wake up call for Make America Great Again (Maga) loyalists who want Trump's political movement to outlast his presidency.

"There's still plenty of Maga voters out there who have supported Donald Trump through thick and thin," said Whit Ayres, a Republican strategist.

"But there is also a significant portion of the Republican Party that's non-Maga, and that's a majority now."

Should Republican hopefuls distance themselves from Trump?

The party lost control of the House and Senate, as well as governorships and state legislatures in red states like Texas and Kansas where Democrats had been shut out of power for decades - and where Trump won by double digits when he was on the ballot.

The stunning upsets underscored the fickle nature of political coalitions.

Trump expanded the Republican base in 2024, increasing support with Latinos and younger voters among other key groups. Republicans hailed the gains as a sign of future strength for the party.

Just two years later, the party lost ground with nearly every critical voting bloc. According to a New York Times analysis of voter data, Latino support for Democratic candidates increased by 29 percentage points from 2024-26. Support from young voters 18-29 years old increased by 33 points.

The swings reflected polling ahead of the midterms that found widespread disapproval with Trump's handling of the economy, immigration and the war with Iran.

Democrats also capitalised on a public perception that the Trump family and administration is rife with self-dealing and corruption. The president's focus on the White House ballroom and other Washington construction projects also contributed to a sense among voters that he was more focused on his legacy than addressing affordability issues.

It's a sentiment shared by Benjamin Shrader, the leader of the Young Republicans in Austin, who was still shell-shocked when he spoke to the BBC in Texas the morning after his party was almost wiped out in the state by a Democratic "blue tsunami".

Shrader said Trump was still a "force of nature" when asked to reflect on how the president had used his first public appearance after the results to show off the White House ballroom project.

He hesitated before adding: "I would focus on issues that are not ballrooms, that are not renaming things. I would focus on what matters."

The evidence in the immediate aftermath of the midterms suggests that Republicans could benefit by distancing themselves from Trump ahead of 2028.

'Vance was the favourite - now the race is wide open'

Vance tried to thread the needle with his midterm assessment blaming the Iran war and calling for a return to "America First." It was a nuanced critique that broke with Trump on an unpopular war, but embraced a broader political brand that remains popular with the Maga base.

Trump's next moves on Iran will be watched closely by the party for their 2028 implications. An escalation would risk fuelling the concerns voiced by Vance and other "America First" proponents.

In his postmortem statement on X, Vance also echoed the growing calls on the right to reexamine US support for Israel. But he also signalled an openness to making some immigration enforcement changes. That clashes with Miller, a Vance ally who has speared the administration's second-term immigration agenda.

Party strategists said the midterm drubbing complicated Vance's path to the nomination.

"Before this midterm, JD Vance was the odds-on favourite to win the Republican nomination in 2028. After this midterm, the nomination battle is completely wide open," Ayres said.

Potential Trump successors have some time to consider their options, but they'll have to make up their minds relatively soon. Any 2028 presidential hopefuls will face pressure to announce White House bids in the next few months. Some could launch campaigns before the end of the year.

Vance's election analysis was widely interpreted as an unofficial signal of his plans to run. It will likely be a crowded primary field.

Other rumoured White House contenders include Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, Florida Governor DeSantis, former US ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, to name a few.

In the next election cycle, Republican presidential and congressional candidates alike will have tough decisions to make on key issues of the day, from US support for Israel to tariffs to the AI boom.

Trump's power may be diminished as he enters the final two years of his second term, but he'll still have the loudest voice in the party over the next two years. It's unclear whether he will get deeply involved in the process or take a hands-off approach.

Trump has praised Vance and Rubio at different times, but typically deflects questions about who he'd like to see succeed him.

His endorsement will loom as the biggest wildcard in the 2028 Republican primary race.

"It remains to be seen who will jump into that race," Ayres said.

"But I think it's going to be a lot larger and more diverse than we anticipated before the midterm election."
